common_name: Quietness Rose (Fragrant Soft Pink Cold-Hardy Own-Root Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Quietness is one of the most popular Griffith Buck-bred roses from Iowa State University, valued for its strong fragrance and cold hardiness on its own roots.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Quietness bears large, double, soft pink blooms with a strong, sweet old-rose fragrance on a compact, bushy, own-root shrub bred at Iowa State University by Griffith Buck for reliable performance through harsh Midwestern winters without winter protection. Among Buck's many introductions, it remains one of the most widely grown for the combination of generous fragrance, gentle color, and dependable rebloom through the growing season. Because it grows on its own roots, winter dieback simply regrows true to type rather than reverting to rootstock, and it needs far less spray intervention than most hybrid teas. Deadhead spent blooms to encourage continued flowering, and prune moderately in late winter to shape the plant.
sources: Iowa State University — Griffith Buck Rose Introductions

common_name: Square Dancer Rose (Pink Blend Cold-Hardy Own-Root Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Square Dancer is a Griffith Buck-bred rose from Iowa State University, prized for cold hardiness on its own roots.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Square Dancer bears double blooms in a blend of pink tones with a light, sweet fragrance on a compact, bushy, own-root shrub bred at Iowa State University by Griffith Buck for reliable performance through harsh Midwestern winters without winter protection. It reblooms through the growing season with only moderate care, tolerating black spot and other common diseases far better than older hybrid teas. Because it grows on its own roots, winter dieback simply regrows true to type rather than reverting to rootstock. Deadhead spent blooms to encourage continued flowering, and prune moderately in late winter to shape the plant.
sources: Iowa State University — Griffith Buck Rose Introductions
